  - comment: Compliance DB confirms Eric Woods (E019) is an Engineer, full-time. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, not Engineer, so admin is not permitted. Full-time employees may have up to write; requested level (write) is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 5 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1, note 2, note 3, note 4)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1, note 2, note 3, note 4)

Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires the role to own the system (Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist, not Engineer). Requested level (write) is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 6 (ticket 1):

  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Eric Woods (E019) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. He has basic training, so maximum is read. Requested write exceeds policy, so recommend read.
reason: The Security database (verified via lookup) shows Eric Woods (E019) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Notes 2–5 did not independently verify employment type; only Note 1 (full_time) and Note 6 (contractor) represent direct lookups, and they conflict. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training—never admin. Since Eric has basic training, his maximum level is read. The requested level (write) exceeds the maximum, so the granted level is read.
